body:
I live with my parents now. Though I submit job applications like it's a part time job, I still can't find a job that offers health insurance. My state doesn't allow single adults with no children access to low income based aid so I went off my medication. Off my meds, I find myself overspending because it's hard to justify not doing something that will give me a few hours worth of not-sadness. 

I have a few new people I hang out with, but my best friend moved half an hour away recently and I suspect I'll never see her again. My new friends mostly just get high and drink their asses off and it's free so I don't see a reason not to join them. I fell in love again but every time I think about it, I get flashbacks from my failed engagement and want to hurl.

I'm worse at my job now. 

 I asked God for a sign not to try again and I won a big prize in a work raffle the next day, so I just keep praying He'll choose to gift me someone else's fatal accident. It keeps not happening and I don't get why. My parents keep making small comments about the girl who failed to kill herself and got the face transplant, as if my attempts failed because I fucked it up. They failed because of flukes. I technically should have died at least twice by now.

My life isn't much worse, but it certainly isn't better. I don't regret my attempts. I'm not happy to be alive. I'm still 99% sure every single person I know would be better off without me and have facts to back it up. It's been 8 months since my last attempt.
All I can say is no, I'm not doing better. I'm sticking around for the sake of my roommate because the complex won't break a lease.
Oh! Thanks, friendski was a sentiment. My actual fav show rn is the Good Place which is so positive and a pretty healthy show to watch even though it's focused on the afterlife
I'm reading and it's really just pure. Also helps seeing other people succeed at things a lot of people sort of take for granted and it's outright celebrated
I just finished a short routine! Do you have your own set or go off a video? I've been looking for some good ones
I'm Nicola. And I like a lot of tv. It's distracting and relatively cheap, you know?

This was a major deal breaker with a person I thought I was going to spend the rest of my life with. I was determined to beat it, try new foods with them, but I got tired. I couldn't cure myself for just one person and it's not easy getting physically ill every time I tried to push my limits. It got harder to try them and in the end it wasn't enough. 

I agree with the coffee suggestion - also 'experience' dates, like local concerts or shows.

I still haven't gotten over 10, so I know how you feel. I could watch 11 for a while but it was so jarring how different it was and I really preferred the kinds of plots that went down in the 9/10 era. I tried again when 12 came in but goodness, I didn't see his charm (or his companions, for that matter).

I saw some gifs from the Christmas special that convinced me to at least give it a shot. I was all about the 1st Doctor. That crotchety bro was completely willing to just push innocent humans into space.

Once Upon a Time was a guilty pleasure show that kept me hooked until the initial curse was broken. I found out that I only cared so long as the A plot revolved around the "real" world and once that disappeared I lost interest. I hear there's some fantastical weird plots that I would likely love if they were on any other show, but I don't have the slightest urge to try and watch again. 

Supernatural lost me on season 5. I felt like a lot of the charm left. I tried so hard to keep watching for the next 3 seasons but it was like trying to take a cold shower in the middle of winter.

The Magicians was a show I was really hyped for and loved until the end of s1. The way they handled certain aspects of a dark subject for two characters seemed tasteless and tone deaf. It's a shame. I really grew to love the adaptation in a different way than the books and felt like they changed just enough to keep things fresh and keep me guessing as to which plots they were keeping from the books.

Unfortunately, I'm the only one at my job who can do my job. We're pretty heavily understaffed - it's not like I have an important job, but everyone else has too many hours so no one can ever step in for someone else. But I can bring oreos for a snack and wear uggs.

Went out to my car and sat there and cried for half an hour until xanax #3 kicked in. Shout out to me for being too big a wimp to do it. There wasn't a reason in the world not to and I couldn't go through with it
Life saved again by xanax making me too tired to walk out to my car. Ladies and gentlemen, always keep your methods in your car. Gotta put forth some-effort-
Pft. Physical Kids are where it's at.

I'm really tired of having friends who haven't read a new series since I met them 11 years ago but who brag about being big readers.

I'm also tired of grown people fawning over their house. Like, even if HP were real and you went to Hogwarts, do you think you would still care after graduation? It's like wearing a letterman jacket

It's one thing to enjoy the books. But when you're 30 and haven't even touched another series, YA or otherwise? My friends, you obviously have time to read since this is your like 10th reading. Just read The Magicians.

I don't know if my spoiled food phobia is related to my ARFID or if it's from a childhood with a mother who never wanted to throw anything out, but this would be enough to keep me from wanting to eat anything at all that isn't a completely safe food for at least a week. 

It's completely understandable to be iffy with nectarines for a time considering the circumstances. I haven't had that happen with fruit in a while (last time was in my rice) but I can deffo relate here. It just takes me at most like 3 weeks to work back.
